title: Slides of ovule development
body: A student examines four permanent slides prepared from ovules of the same flowering plant at different stages. Slide P shows a single large cell with dense cytoplasm and a prominent nucleus in the micropylar region of the nucellus. Slide Q shows four cells arranged in a row; three of them appear to be degenerating. Slide R shows a sac-like cell containing four nuclei, two near each end, with no cell walls between them. Slide S shows a structure with three cells grouped at the micropylar end, three cells at the chalazal end and a large central cell containing two nuclei.

title: How long can seeds stay alive?
body: As a seed matures, its water content falls to about 10-15 per cent moisture by mass and the general metabolic activity of the embryo slows down. The embryo may enter a state of inactivity called dormancy, or, if adequate moisture, oxygen and a suitable temperature are available, the seed germinates. The period for which seeds remain alive varies greatly: some lose viability within a few months, many live for several years, and a few have remained alive for centuries. A seed of the lupine Lupinus arcticus excavated from the Arctic tundra germinated after an estimated 10,000 years of dormancy, and a 2000-year-old seed of the date palm Phoenix dactylifera was found viable during an archaeological excavation near the Dead Sea. Farmers store seeds harvested in one season to raise the crop in the next.

title: The cost of hybrid seed
body: Hybrid varieties of many food and vegetable crops are now widely cultivated because they give much higher yields. A farmer, however, has to buy fresh hybrid seed every year. If seeds collected from a hybrid crop are sown, the plants of the next generation segregate and do not keep the hybrid characters. Producing hybrid seed is costly, so the seed is expensive for farmers. Some species of Asteraceae and grasses produce seeds without fertilisation, a process called apomixis. Laboratories around the world are studying the genetics of apomixis and trying to transfer apomictic genes into hybrid varieties.
